doc: FBL 0.9's grammar family reading a body in part (section 4.9, recover): the string on line 5 has no closing quote, so reading stops at its quote; the statement is skipped from its first byte to the '.' that ends it, kept and reported once as fbl.unparsed-text at line 5, and the statements before and after it are read (story 7 scenario 3 of spec 035).

steps.doc: An add into a body read in part: after the last resource, ex:bob; the skipped statement is kept byte for byte and still reported (FBL 4.9).
Undo puts back the bytes the edit replaced.
A removal of the resource above the skipped statement takes only its own line; the skipped text, which binds nothing, is not touched.
Undo puts back the bytes the edit replaced.
